result.rule: Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Lanes may be nested: a lane can contain a child laneSet that partitions it further; every flowNodeRef at any depth references nodes of the one owning process.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

result.rule: When the description names two distinct responsible parties, a human user who makes the choices and an automated component that carries out the later work, and both are needed in the same process: Model the process as one participant pool with one lane per named responsible party (a lane for the user and a separate lane for the automated component). Place each activity and event in the lane of the party that performs it: the user's initiating event and choice-gathering steps in the user lane, and the autonomous execution step in the automated component's lane. Do not omit these lanes, and do not put the automated work in a start event; model the work as a task in the automated lane.

When The description names a role or department that performs at least one activity or decision, even when it is mentioned only in one clause among other roles' activities.: Create a lane for each such role inside the owning pool, and place every activity, event and gateway that this role performs in that role's lane. Do not omit a role's lane because its activity is secondary or appears in a single clause.

When the description says that a request made in one system starts a separate process in another system, and that this started process is the one that exchanges messages with an outside party: Model the started process as its own participant pool. Give that pool a message start event and draw a message flow from the requesting task in the requesting pool to this message start event. Do not connect the two systems with a sequence flow or a plain start event.

When the description says the process starts when an actor submits something (a request, order or application) that the actor does before the process's own work begins: Model a start event for the process trigger, and model the submitting action itself as a separate task performed by that actor, placed directly after the start event and in the actor's lane or pool when one is given. Do not use the start event to represent the submitting action, and do not label the start event with the submitted result.
